tierWindow.goal: Put citation into action: bring sources into your own writing accurately, build correct references, and apply a referencing style consistently.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Application and construction (select, construct, apply, integrate), beyond the recognition and description of the introductory tier.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Realistic tasks with a few moving parts at once: choosing quotation or paraphrase, placing a citation, assembling a reference from its elements, applying one style across a list.
tierWindow.autonomy: Moderate scaffolding; worked examples show a weaker and a stronger attempt; the learner then makes the moves, with checks that test a choice rather than a definition.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already knows what referencing is and why it matters in principle (the introductory tier), and has met in-text references and a reference list without yet producing them reliably. They are now writing assignments that must cite sources, so the course teaches the doing: quoting and paraphrasing with citations, building accurate references, and applying a style consistently.

subThemes.label: In-text citation: acknowledging a source at the point you use it
Quotation and paraphrase: two ways to bring a source in, and when each fits
The anatomy of a reference: the elements it is built from and their fixed order
Formatting references for different source types: books, journal articles and web pages
Accuracy: building a reliable reference list and avoiding copy-and-paste errors
Referencing styles: selecting one suited to your discipline and applying it consistently
Citation as a tool: evidencing the scope and critical edge of your research against marking criteria

decidedValue.courseOutcomeCountReason: Three, matching the three intermediate sub-strands of citation in action: bringing sources into your writing (in-text citation, quotation and paraphrase), building the reference list accurately (constructing references for each source type), and applying a style with purpose (consistency, and citation as evidence against marking criteria). decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, citing as you write: quoting and paraphrasing a source, with the citation in the right place. Second, building accurate references: assembling a reference for a book, a journal article and a web page. Third, working with referencing styles: choosing one, applying it consistently, and using citation to meet marking criteria. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This course is about citing sources in your own work: bringing them in accurately, building a reference list that holds up, and applying a referencing style with purpose. You already know what referencing is and why it matters. This course is about doing it well.

Citation is a practical skill you use in almost every assignment. Quote or paraphrase a source and you must cite it; list that source correctly at the end; keep one style across the whole piece. Get this right and your work reads as careful, honest and well-researched, and it earns marks against the criteria.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: integrate sources through in-text citation, construct accurate references, and apply a style consistently to meet marking criteria.

practiceConnection.academic: Citation runs through everything you write at university. Every essay that draws on reading, every report that cites data, every dissertation with a reference list, depends on citing sources accurately and consistently. Getting it right protects your academic integrity and shows a marker the scope of your research. The same care carries into professional work, where sourcing a claim well is part of being trusted.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the advanced referencing course takes you into academic integrity as a scholarly value, handling data and sources ethically, and citing with judgement in complex work. Going wider: the same skills support Academic Writing, Finding and Using Sources, and Researching and Research Methods, where citation is put to work on real tasks.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Citation is now something you can do with purpose, not just recognise. You can bring a source into your writing by quoting or paraphrasing, and cite it correctly either way. You can build an accurate reference for a book, a journal article or a web page. And you can apply a referencing style consistently, using your reference list to show a marker the scope and care of your research. Look back at the confidence check to see how far you have moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, citation is part of almost every piece of work you submit. Each essay, report and dissertation asks you to bring in sources, reference them accurately, and keep one style throughout. Done well, it protects your academic integrity and earns marks against the criteria. The same habit of sourcing a claim carefully carries into professional work, where trust depends on it.
